levels.description: The floor of the scale. Papers, trials, price curves and open releases are all moving slower than BLISS calls normal. That is not a judgement about whether anything good is happening — it is a quiet hour on these particular instruments.
levels.gloss: Upside activity below this index’s own historical norm.
levels.name: BECALMED

levels.description: The scale is centred here by construction: 50 is the middle of the frozen reference distribution. A reading in this band means nothing across the five pillars is behaving out of character.
levels.gloss: Upside activity within the normal range of the record.
levels.name: STEADY

levels.description: Something is carrying the average. One or more pillars have pulled clear of their own reference distribution and the composite followed. It says louder than usual. It does not say why, and the pillar breakdown is where you go to find out.
levels.gloss: Upside activity above the normal range of the record.
levels.name: LIFTING

levels.description: The top decile, with several pillars high at once. That is what it looks like when results, trials and open releases land in the same window — and it is also what it looks like when one source is having a strange week. The inputs tell them apart.
levels.gloss: Upside activity in the top decile of the record.
levels.name: SURGING

levels.description: Past the top of the reference distribution: the frozen record holds nothing like this. The name is a statement about our own record running out, not about anybody being saved. Those are two different sentences and this index refuses to merge them.
levels.epithet: Off the top of the chart
levels.gloss: Upside activity beyond anything in the record.
levels.name: UNMATCHED

pillars.blurb: AI methods showing up in other people’s fields.
pillars.description: Papers outside computer science whose method is a model: structural biology, materials, chemistry, numerical analysis. Not the field talking about itself — the field being used by somebody solving a different problem.
pillars.name: Science

pillars.description: Registered interventional trials involving AI, and the published clinical literature pairing a model with a diagnosis. A trial costs a protocol, an ethics board and enrolled human beings. It is the most expensive signal in this index.
pillars.name: Medicine

pillars.blurb: What a dollar buys, and what you may keep.
pillars.description: The price of a million tokens at the cheap frontier, the volume of weights published under a licence that lets a stranger run them commercially without asking, and the share of Hub uploads that carry that licence. Falling cost is not a proxy for broadening access. It is broadening access.
pillars.name: Access

pillars.description: Installs of the AI stack and downloads of widely deployed open models. Every other pillar counts what laboratories produce; this one counts what everybody else does with it.
pillars.name: Adoption

pillars.blurb: How much of it anybody is allowed to hold.
pillars.description: The open-weight share of notable model releases over a year, and the count of new permissively licensed ML repositories over a month. One measures the frontier, the other the floor. A share can fall while every count rises, and this pillar can say so.
pillars.name: Openness
